ci.yml.plan-test:
name: the planner's own test
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'plan-test')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - run: python3 ci/tiers-test.py
      - run: python3 ci/is80/dist-test.py
      - name: pinned anchor keys agree both ways
        run: python3 ci/is81-variadic/anchors.py

  # Primary gate: linux/x86-64 runs the whole ladder, including the corpus walk.
  # macOS/aarch64 and windows/x86-64 build and test (D35 posture).
  #
  # EVERY OS IS SHARDED. Windows first (wolf-interp#121): `cargo test` on
  # windows-latest is 29,267 s — 8 h 08 m, measured at 552786e — against
  # GitHub's 6 h job cap, which `timeout-minutes` can lower but never raise,
  # so the leg was *cancelled* and wolf-interp had no windows coverage at all.
  # Then linux and macOS (wolf-interp#123, is57): at 0cfc0cf the unsharded
  # linux job was cancelled at its 355-minute timeout on BOTH attempts of the
  # trunk push (jobs 108652393221, 108714531246, 355.3 min each), and macOS
  # took 341.3 of 355 minutes on the PR run of the same tree (job
  # 108596027284). Each OS now runs three test shards plus one job for the
  # process-level ladder and the bundle; at 0cfc0cf the widest shard is 95
  # min of test time on linux and 107 on macOS, the ladder 76 and 66.
  #
  # The step bodies below are shared by every entry — one copy, selected with
  # `if:` — so a shard can never drift from another OS's.
  #
  # The shard key lives in `ci/test-shards.sh` and is a function of the target
  # NAME alone, so a failure names the same shard twice. Coverage is not
  # asserted here: `shards cover the suite`, below, proves from cargo's own
  # output that each OS's shards ran every declared target exactly once, and
  # no test twice.
  #
  # EVERY JOB HAS `timeout-minutes`. A cancelled job reads as infrastructure;
  # a failed one reads as "this leg does not fit", which is the thing a
  # reader needs to know. 330 is under the 6 h ceiling and about three times
  # the widest shard. A smoke's 30 is its budget: is75 set 20, and the
  # windows smoke grew to 19 m 40 s and was cancelled at it twice with
  # nothing failed (wolf-interp#215, #226), so r32 raised it.
  #
  # The entries come from `plan` (is75, is78): on a release run, os × {1,
  # 2, 3, ladder} for ubuntu, macOS and windows — the twelve entries and job
  # names of before — and the windows smoke; on a full run and a PR run
  # ubuntu's four plus `smoke` on macOS and windows (tl29: macOS's four
  # left the merge as windows's did in is78).
  #
  # Measured whole-job times, kept from before the matrix moved into `plan`:
  # linux at 0cfc0cf (job 108596027245): 5,691 / 5,654 / 5,137 s of
  # test time for shards 1 / 2 / 3; 4,578 s of ladder steps.
  # macOS at 0cfc0cf (job 108596027284): 6,405 / 4,892 / 5,161 s;
  # 3,941 s of ladder steps.
  # windows at 0cfc0cf (run 36310738129): 170.7 / 113.7 / 155.1 min
  # whole-job for shards 1 / 2 / 3 and 135.6 min for the ladder.
  # A ladder entry runs the steps after `cargo test`: the corpus walk, the
  # conform-run rungs, the explorer, the fixtures, the differential lane,
  # the fuzz smoke, the place-trace identity and the bundle. A smoke runs
  # the build-and-test step over the smoke's targets and the five fast
  # ladder steps (the rungs, explorer, fixtures, differential lane, fuzz
  # smoke); never the corpus walk, the place-trace identity or the bundle,
  # which are 40 + 7 + 40 minutes on windows.
ci.yml.test:
name: >-
      test (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.shard == 'ladder' && 'the ladder and the bundle'
      || matrix.shard == 'smoke' && 'smoke'
      || format('test shard {0} of 3', matrix.shard) }})
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'test')
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.shard == 'smoke' && 30 || 330 }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix || '[]') }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
          # `upstream/` is the pinned wolf-lang submodule (PRIVATE — CI uses
          # the tracked vendor/upstream snapshot instead; vendor/README.md).
          # The gitlink pin stays visible via `git submodule status --cached`.
          # code. The whole harness is dark without it.

      # The runner image ships some toolchain; `rust-toolchain.toml` names the
      # one we test against. Install it explicitly — an implicit rustup
      # proxy-install races the first cargo invocation and picks up neither
      # rustfmt nor clippy.
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: |
          rustup show active-toolchain
          rustup component add rustfmt clippy

      - name: Toolchain versions
        run: |
          rustc --version
          cargo --version
          cargo fmt --version
          cargo clippy --version

      - name: rustfmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

      # A numbered shard passes the argument list `ci/test-shards.sh` derives
      # from its stable key; that script refuses to emit an EMPTY list, since
      # an empty one would make `cargo test` silently run everything — a shard
      # that looks like a fast pass while being the thing we are sharding.
      # `--doc` cannot share an invocation with a target flag, so the shard
      # that owns the doc-tests runs them second, into the same log.
      #
      # The log is `tee`d (not `| grep`ed — that is the EPIPE trap) so the
      # step can read back WHICH binaries and WHICH tests ran from cargo's own
      # output. That measurement, not the table in the script, is what the
      # coverage job compares; the per-test count is reconciled against
      # cargo's `test result:` totals before it is uploaded.
      #
      # A smoke (is75) passes every target except SMOKE_OMITS, through the
      # same script, and runs the doc-tests unless `doc` is omitted.
      # is77 (wolf-interp#263): `tests/core_is77.rs`'s cores-on row needs a
      # FILE core pattern, so a core is written in the container's working
      # directory, the test's own, and removed there (the runner's default
      # pipes to a program). Set on this throwaway runner only; the runner's
      # own `ulimit -c` is left as it is, and every linux job sets
      # LUPIN_CORE_REQUIRE below, so the row's skip is a failure here.
      - name: a file core pattern for is77's core witness (#263)
        if: matrix.osid == 'ubuntu' && matrix.shard != 'ladder'
        run: |
          echo "core_pattern was: $(cat /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern)"
          echo 'core.%p' | sudo tee /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern
          echo "ulimit -c on the runner: $(ulimit -c)"
          docker run --rm --network none docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04 sh -c 'echo "in a container: ulimit -c $(ulimit -c), hard $(ulimit -Hc)"'

      - name: test
        if: matrix.shard != 'ladder'
        shell: bash
        env:
          LUPIN_CORE_REQUIRE: ${{ matrix.osid == 'ubuntu' && '1' || '0' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "the shard key, for the whole crate:"
          ci/test-shards.sh plan
          if [ '${{ matrix.shard }}' = smoke ]; then
            echo "the smoke omits (SMOKE_OMITS): $SMOKE_OMITS"
            args=$(ci/test-shards.sh smoke-args $SMOKE_OMITS)
            case " $SMOKE_OMITS " in *" doc "*) doc=no ;; *) doc=yes ;; esac
          else
            args=$(ci/test-shards.sh args '${{ matrix.shard }}')
            if ci/test-shards.sh has-doc '${{ matrix.shard }}'; then doc=yes; else doc=no; fi
          fi
          echo "shard ${{ matrix.shard }} runs: $args"
          cargo test $args 2>&1 | tee test-output.log
          if [ "$doc" = yes ]; then
            echo "shard ${{ matrix.shard }} runs the doc-tests: cargo test --doc"
            cargo test --doc 2>&1 | tee -a test-output.log
          fi
          ci/test-shards.sh ran test-output.log > test-binaries.txt
          ci/test-shards.sh tests test-output.log > test-names.txt
          ci/test-shards.sh tests-check test-output.log
          echo "this job ran $(wc -l < test-binaries.txt) test binaries:"
          cat test-binaries.txt

      # A smoke's listing is printed above and not uploaded: it is not a
      # shard, and `shards cover the suite` checks shards.
      - name: upload the test binaries and tests this job ran
        if: matrix.shard != 'ladder' && matrix.shard != 'smoke'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: test-binaries-${{ matrix.osid }}-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: |
            test-binaries.txt
            test-names.txt
          if-no-files-found: error

      # A green walk means every corpus directive header is legible to our own
      # directive parser.
      - name: corpus harness
        if: matrix.shard == 'ladder'
        run: cargo run -- corpus

      # The ladder, end to end through the real binary rather than the library:
      # `conform-run` is a *process* contract ([proto.invoke.exit]). Each check
      # below pins one rung of the mapping documented in `src/frontend.rs`:
      #
      #   lex / parse      is01's frontend
      #   resolve          is02's sema-lite (module graph, visibility)
      #   typecheck/mem/wir  NOT performed — `unsupported` at `resolve`
      #   run              is02's tree-walk evaluator, is03's region machine,
      #                    is04's provenance machine and UB oracle
      #
      # A record that claims a rung this implementation did not complete is the
      # exact failure [proto.record.phase] exists to prevent, so the assertions
      # are on `phase_reached` as much as on `verdict`.
      #
      # Discipline, learned the hard way on macOS: **capture, then grep.** A
      # direct `cmd | grep -q` closes the pipe the moment grep matches, and the
      # writer's flush then races the close and aborts with EPIPE. Every check
      # below assigns to a variable first.
      - name: conform-run rungs
        if: matrix.shard == 'ladder' || matrix.shard == 'smoke'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          fail=0
          # The corpus's own LEXICAL counter-examples need no list here.
          # A ledger `phase: none` means no rung completed, and the ladder's
          # shallowest rung is `lex`, so such a file is refused BY the lexer
          # and its `check: fail(CODE)` names the code the corpus pins.
          # Everything else must lex clean.
          #
          # wolf-interp#58: this step and `tests/lex_corpus.rs` each used to
          # keep a hand-written list of those files, so every by-design lex
          # refusal that arrived with a pin reddened CI twice. Both readers
          # now derive the set from the same place — the directive header the
          # corpus file carries. Do not reintroduce a name here.
          while IFS= read -r f; do
            out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run "$f" --phase=lex --json)
            phase=$(sed -n 's|^//! *phase: *\([a-z]*\).*|\1|p' "$f" | head -1)
            if [[ "$phase" == none ]]; then
              code=$(sed -n 's|^//! *check: *fail(\([A-Z][0-9]*\)).*|\1|p' "$f" | head -1)
              if [[ -z "$code" ]]; then
                echo "::error file=$f::a phase-none ledger with no check: fail(CODE)"; fail=1; continue
              fi
              want="\"verdict\":\"fail($code)\""
            else
              want='"verdict":"pass"'
            fi
            if [[ "$out" == *"$want"* && "$out" == *'"phase_reached":"lex"'* ]]; then :; else
              # Ruling #28 (`[proto.record.first]`; wolf-interp#175): a
              # `phase: lex` row may carry a lexical fault AFTER the parse
              # refusal it pins — the record is the earliest diagnostic
              # (`rows/negative/first_parse_before_lex.lu`,
              # `first_boundary_before_lex.lu`, the 8e36bc1a pin). The same
              # derivation as `tests/lex_corpus.rs` and
              # `tests/conformance.rs`: the ledger phase and the `check:`
              # code, no name.
              if [[ "$phase" == lex ]]; then
                code=$(sed -n 's|^//! *check: *fail(\([A-Z][0-9]*\)).*|\1|p' "$f" | head -1)
                parsed=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run "$f" --phase=parse --json)
                lex_at=$(echo "$out" | sed -n 's|.*"span":\[\([0-9]*\),.*|\1|p' | head -1)
                parse_at=$(echo "$parsed" | sed -n 's|.*"span":\[\([0-9]*\),.*|\1|p' | head -1)
                if [[ -n "$code" && "$parsed" == *"\"verdict\":\"fail($code)\""* \
                      && -n "$lex_at" && -n "$parse_at" && "$parse_at" -lt "$lex_at" ]]; then
                  continue
                fi
              fi
              echo "::error file=$f::lex rung is not clean: $out"; fail=1
            fi
          done < <(find vendor/upstream/corpus -name '*.lu' | sort)
          test "$fail" -eq 0

          # parse: the canonical program is clean, a counter-example carries its
          # pinned code (and the tool still exits 0).
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/wordcount.lu --phase=parse --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"pass"'
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/grammar/structlit_cond.lu --phase=parse --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"fail(E0006)"'

          # resolve: sema-lite completes on every well-formed file.
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/regions.lu --phase=resolve --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"resolve","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"pass"'

          # typecheck: NOT performed. The honest answer is the deepest completed
          # rung plus `unsupported` — never a claim of `typecheck`.
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/hello.lu --phase=typecheck --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"resolve","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"unsupported"'

          # run: files from the first-run ledger, by verdict — one per rung of
          # the trap vocabulary this implementation reaches.
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/hello.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"run","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"exit\(0\)"'
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/hello.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"stdout_inline":"hello, wolf'
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/overflow.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"trap(overflow)"'
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/memory/div_zero.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"trap(div-zero)"'

          # is03's Tier-1/2 rungs: the region litmuses run, and the generational
          # handle fault is `stale-handle` in every profile ([mem.shared.handle.2]).
          for f in region_ambient_ok region_multiopen_ok region_multiopen_swap \
                   region_iso_edge_ok shared_ok; do
            out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run "vendor/upstream/corpus/memory/$f.lu" --json)
            echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"run","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"exit\(0\)"' \
              || { echo "::error::memory/$f.lu no longer reaches run cleanly"; exit 1; }
          done
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/memory/handle_stale.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"trap(stale-handle)"'

          # is04's Tier-3 rungs. The unsafe litmuses became runnable when the
          # provenance machine landed: a *true* `assume noalias` is defined
          # ([mem.unsafe.raw.2]), and the use-after-free one is the oracle's
          # verdict rather than a trap ([proto.record.verdict]).
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/memory/unsafe_noalias.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"run","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"exit\(0\)"'
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/memory/unsafe_ub_uaf.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"run","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"ub\(mem.ub\)"'
          # [proto.record.ub]: the row id rides `x-ub-row`, and the D2 pairing —
          # the optimization the row licenses — rides the record too, because a
          # UB rule that licenses nothing is one this language does not have.
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"x-ub-row":"P1"'
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"x-ub-licenses":"O1:'
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"x-ub-clause":"mem.prov.state"'

          # Every §7 row this tier detects, from the authored programs, with the
          # near-miss twin proving the check discriminates. `tests/ub_coverage.rs`
          # is the matrix; this is the same claim through the process contract.
          # P1's witness is the corpus (memory/unsafe_ub_uaf.lu, checked
          # by the run-rung block above); the protector shape is a unit
          # test (tests/prov_machine.rs) since the v0.1.5 suite rebuild.
          # T1 retired to Unreachable at v0.1.5 (as-bool is a static
          # rejection now); the loop is the directory's actual contents.
          for row in p2_frozen_write p3_out_of_bounds p4_region_freed \
                     p5_false_noalias p6_false_door l1_uninitialized l2_dangling; do
            id=$(echo "$row" | cut -c1-2 | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')
            out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run "tests/ub/$row.lu" --json)
            echo "$out" | grep -q "\"verdict\":\"ub(mem.ub)\"" \
              || { echo "::error::tests/ub/$row.lu no longer reports UB: $out"; exit 1; }
            echo "$out" | grep -q "\"x-ub-row\":\"$id\"" \
              || { echo "::error::tests/ub/$row.lu reports the wrong row: $out"; exit 1; }
          done
          while IFS= read -r f; do
            out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run "$f" --json)
            echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"run","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"exit\(0\)"' \
              || { echo "::error::$f is a near-miss twin and must run clean: $out"; exit 1; }
          done < <(find tests/ub/ok -name '*.lu' | sort)

          # The `faults/` and `comptime/` tiers that arrived with the pin.
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/faults/overflow_add.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"trap(overflow)"'
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/comptime/norm_linear.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"run","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"exit\(0\)"'

          # `--trace=mem` is a filter over the rule registry: every line it
          # keeps cites a `mem.*` clause, and the region events are all there.
          trace=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run \
            vendor/upstream/corpus/memory/region_multiopen_ok.lu --trace=mem 2>&1 >/dev/null)
          echo "$trace" | grep -q 'RegionMultiopen \[mem.region.multiopen\]'
          if echo "$trace" | grep '^trace ' | grep -v '\[mem\.' ; then
            echo "::error::--trace=mem leaked a non-memory rule"; exit 1
          fi

          # `--trace=prov` is the same mechanism one tier up: the Tier-3 subset,
          # §5 `mem.unsafe.*` + §6 `mem.prov.*` + §7 `mem.ub*`, plus the FFI
          # boundary clause. Derived from the anchor, never a hand-kept list.
          # protector trace lines are pinned by tests/prov_machine.rs in
          # the test lane; here the licensed-pairing and namespace checks
          # run on a current suite file.
          trace=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run tests/ub/p4_region_freed.lu \
            --trace=prov 2>&1 >/dev/null)
          echo "$trace" | grep -q 'UbLicensed \[mem.ub.closed\]'
          if echo "$trace" | grep '^trace ' \
               | grep -vE '\[mem\.(prov|unsafe|ub|boundary)' ; then
            echo "::error::--trace=prov leaked a non-Tier-3 rule"; exit 1
          fi

          # "Zero UB in safe code" as a process assertion, not only a library
          # one: the unsafe-free litmuses never produce a `ub(*)` verdict.
          for f in memory/prov_holy_grail memory/prov_two_phase memory/region_multiopen_swap \
                   memory/shared_ok wordcount hello; do
            out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run "vendor/upstream/corpus/$f.lu" --json)
            if echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"ub('; then
              echo "::error::$f.lu is safe-tier and reached a §7 row: $out"; exit 1
            fi
          done

          # A file outside coverage says so, with a reason on an `x-` key
          # ([proto.record.ext]) rather than in the payload-free verdict.
          # S-5 repaired upstream (s20): `procs.lu` is self-contained and RUNS.
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/procs.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"exit(0)"'

          # is06's spec/03 rungs: the conc litmus tier runs under the sim
          # scheduler. Unseeded records declare seeded:false and run FIFO.
          for f in conc/cancel_sibling conc/message_passing conc/select_seeded; do
            out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run "vendor/upstream/corpus/$f.lu" --json)
            echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"run","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"exit\(0\)"'               || { echo "::error::$f.lu no longer reaches run cleanly: $out"; exit 1; }
          done
          # `--seed=N` requests the spec/03 §5 deterministic schedule, the
          # record declares it ([proto.seed.flag]), and the same seed replays
          # the identical record ([conc.det.seed]).
          one=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/conc/select_seeded.lu --seed=7 --json)
          echo "$one" | grep -q '"seeded":true'
          two=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/conc/select_seeded.lu --seed=7 --json)
          test "$one" = "$two"
          # The E1005 dynamic-counterpart case finally RUNS (`channel` exists):
          # the open region cannot transfer — region-fault per [conf.trap.map].
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/memory/region_move_while_open.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"trap(region-fault)"'
          # `ffi.lu` now *executes* its unsafe block — the C intrinsics are
          # modelled (docs/approximation-contract.md §8) — and stops at the
          # inline `asm`, which no pinned document gives a meaning. Since
          # is70 (wolf-interp#174, `[gram.item.attr.cfg]`) that asm is read
          # through its `#[cfg(target = …)]`; at the 8e36bc1a pin (r28,
          # wolf-lang e951afbb) the row carries an x86_64 and an aarch64
          # variant, so every host keeps exactly one and declines it by name.
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/ffi.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '"verdict":"unsupported",.*asm' \
            || { echo "::error::ffi.lu keeps one asm variant on every host and declines it by name: $out"; exit 1; }
          # `regions.lu` RUNS at pin 8b04edf: the tail now uses only specified
          # semantics (frozen data readable forever, [mem.region.freeze.1]),
          # closing the rest of is03's §5.5 finding. The seed corpus's flagship
          # memory program reaching `run` was two pins in the making — keep it.
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/regions.lu --json)
          echo "$out" | grep -Eq '"phase_reached":"run","seeded":false,"diagnostics":\[\],("warnings":\[\],)?"verdict":"exit\(0\)"'

      # is07: the schedule explorer, bounded, over the whole conc litmus tier
      # — verdict stability (the DRF-SC promise, D14) as a process assertion
      # on all three OSes. The budgets close the frontier on this corpus (the
      # library tests pin the exact schedule counts); here the process-level
      # half: green exit, a stable report, and the replay doors.
      - name: schedule explorer (bounded)
        if: matrix.shard == 'ladder' || matrix.shard == 'smoke'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          # The E11xx fail files are REFUSED by the unified admission
          # ladder since v0.1.7 (#22): explore refuses what run refuses.
          for f in chan_unsendable store_buffer; do
            set +e
            out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run "vendor/upstream/corpus/conc/$f.lu" --explore=500 2>&1)
            code=$?
            set -e
            test "$code" -eq 2 \
              || { echo "::error::conc/$f.lu must be refused at admission (got $code)"; exit 1; }
            echo "$out" | grep -qE 'E110[123]' \
              || { echo "::error::conc/$f.lu refusal must name its E11xx code: $out"; exit 1; }
          done
          for f in cancel_sibling freeze_publish message_passing \
                   proc_kill_defers select_seeded when_multi; do
            out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run "vendor/upstream/corpus/conc/$f.lu" --explore=500) \
              || { echo "::error::conc/$f.lu failed exploration: $out"; exit 1; }
            echo "$out" | grep -q 'observably deterministic' \
              || { echo "::error::conc/$f.lu is schedule-dependent: $out"; exit 1; }
            echo "$out" | grep -q 'frontier closed' \
              || { echo "::error::conc/$f.lu: the budget must close the frontier"; exit 1; }
          done
          # The multiopen model check: the file its own header flags for is07.
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/memory/region_multiopen_ok.lu --explore=100)
          echo "$out" | grep -q 'observably deterministic'
          # The explicit decision-stream replay door is byte-deterministic and
          # declares itself seeded ([proto.seed.equal]).
          one=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/conc/select_seeded.lu --schedule=ev:1 --json)
          two=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/conc/select_seeded.lu --schedule=ev:1 --json)
          test "$one" = "$two"
          echo "$one" | grep -q '"seeded":true'
          # And the naive-DFS baseline agrees with DPOR on a litmus with real
          # branching — identical conclusions, only the counts may differ.
          dpor=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/conc/cancel_sibling.lu --explore=500 --json)
          naive=$(cargo run --quiet -- conform-run vendor/upstream/corpus/conc/cancel_sibling.lu --explore=500 --explore-naive --json)
          echo "$dpor"  | grep -q '"stable":true'
          echo "$naive" | grep -q '"stable":true'

      # The fixtures are the protocol's own tests ([proto.harness.fixtures]).
      - name: protocol fixtures
        if: matrix.shard == 'ladder' || matrix.shard == 'smoke'
        run: |
          cargo run -- protocol validate vendor/upstream/corpus/protocol/valid.json vendor/upstream/corpus/protocol/with-extensions.json

      # The is05 differential lane. CI has no counterparty by construction —
      # the vendored snapshot ships no crates/ and the private submodule
      # cannot clone — so the lane must SKIP *loudly*: structured detection,
      # `notice:` lines naming what was tried and why that is expected, exit
      # 0. `--require-counterparty` is the hard-fail form for environments
      # that promise a compiler (nightly local runs; the wolf-lang side from
      # s23). Both behaviors are asserted, not assumed.
      - name: differential lane (SKIP without a counterparty)
        if: matrix.shard == 'ladder' || matrix.shard == 'smoke'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- diff-run 2>&1) || {
            echo "::error::diff-run must exit 0 when it SKIPs"; exit 1; }
          echo "$out" | grep -q 'notice: differential lane SKIPPED'
          echo "$out" | grep -q 'notice: tried'
          echo "$out" | grep -q 'cargo build -p wolf_driver'
          if cargo run --quiet -- diff-run --require-counterparty 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::--require-counterparty must hard-fail without a compiler"; exit 1
          fi

      # A bounded, seeded fuzz smoke in self-oracle mode: defined-by-
      # construction programs must exit 0; no unsafe-free program may report
      # ub. The full campaign (10k+, against a built counterparty) is a
      # local/nightly affair — its record lives in docs/divergence-log.md.
      - name: fuzz smoke (self-oracle)
        if: matrix.shard == 'ladder' || matrix.shard == 'smoke'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- fuzz --count 100 --seed 5381 --compiler does/not/exist 2>&1)
          echo "$out" | grep -q '0 finding(s)'

      # is72: the place trace never changes a program. Every vendored corpus
      # file runs through the RELEASE binary with `--trace-places` off and
      # on, and stdout, stderr and the exit code must be byte-identical
      # (a debug build took 25 minutes for memory/ alone in process). The
      # script prints the counts and a digest of its per-file ledger.
      - name: place trace identity (release, whole corpus)
        if: matrix.shard == 'ladder'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo build --release --quiet
          bin=target/release/lupin
          [ -f "$bin.exe" ] && bin="$bin.exe"
          ci/place-trace-identity.sh "$bin"

      # is09: the conformance bundle. Determinism is the artifact's whole
      # warranty (docs/conformance-bundle.md), so it is asserted three ways:
      # export twice and byte-compare; run the consumption dry-run (the full
      # pull → verify → diff path, with the bundle's own recorded reference
      # outcomes replayed as the counterparty); and ship the manifest as an
      # artifact so the `bundle-identical` job below can prove the three
      # OSes exported the SAME bundle, hash for hash. The per-file hash
      # listing is printed here so a cross-OS mismatch is diagnosable from
      # the logs alone.
      - name: conformance bundle (determinism + dry run)
        if: matrix.shard == 'ladder'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          cargo run --quiet -- conformance export --out target/bundle-a --json | tee bundle-a.json
          cargo run --quiet -- conformance export --out target/bundle-b >/dev/null
          if ! diff -r target/bundle-a target/bundle-b; then
            echo "::error::re-export is not byte-identical on ${{ matrix.os }}"; exit 1
          fi
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -- conformance check target/bundle-a \
                  --replay target/bundle-a/expected/records.jsonl)
          echo "$out" | grep -q 'divergences: 0' \
            || { echo "::error::the consumption dry-run diverged: $out"; exit 1; }
          echo "bundle_sha256 on ${{ matrix.os }}:"
          grep '"bundle_sha256"' target/bundle-a/MANIFEST.json
          echo "the manifest (per-file hashes — the cross-OS diagnostic):"
          cat target/bundle-a/MANIFEST.json

      # Keep both observations even when their byte comparison fails. The
      # manifests locate a differing file; these records name its fields.
      - name: upload bundle records
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.shard == 'ladder' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: bundle-records-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: |
            target/bundle-a/MANIFEST.json
            target/bundle-a/expected/records.jsonl
            target/bundle-b/MANIFEST.json
            target/bundle-b/expected/records.jsonl
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: upload bundle manifest
        if: matrix.shard == 'ladder'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: bundle-manifest-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: target/bundle-a/MANIFEST.json
          if-no-files-found: error

  # The proof that sharding did not quietly drop a target or a test.
  #
  # Three green shards are exactly what a hole looks like, so this job does
  # not read the shard table: it compares what each OS's shards' `cargo test`
  # runs REPORTED running against the crate's own target list — set equality
  # in both directions, no binary in two shards, no test in two shards — and
  # names the offenders when they disagree. It is r20's hand count, 1 + 2 +
  # 47 = 50, made automatic for every OS. The self-test plants a hole and a
  # double in a copy of the artifacts and passes only if both are refused by
  # name, so this gate is seen red on every run.
  #
  # On a PR run and a full run only ubuntu is sharded (is75, tl29), so the
  # plan names the OSes to check; on a release run it is all three, as
  # every full run was before is78.
ci.yml.shard-coverage:
name: shards cover the suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    needs: [plan, test]
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'shard-coverage')
    env:
      # Read with a default (all three, the script's own): an output that
      # went missing must check more, never less.
      SHARD_OSES: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.shard_oses || 'ubuntu macos windows' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: test-binaries-*
          path: artifacts
      - name: each OS's three shards are a partition of the whole suite
        run: ci/assert-shard-coverage.sh artifacts
      - name: the assertion refuses a planted hole and a planted double
        run: ci/assert-shard-coverage.sh self-test artifacts

  # is09: the three OSes must export the SAME bundle — every normalization
  # lesson (LF-before-observation, slash paths, sorted walks) cashed in as
  # one assertion. The manifests carry a sha256 per file, so on mismatch the
  # diff below names the exact files that differ, and the per-OS job logs
  # above carry the full hash listings.
  #
  # Release runs only (is75, tl29): a PR run and a full run export the
  # bundle on ubuntu alone, and one manifest has nothing to be identical
  # to. Skipped by design there. The plan names the OSes whose ladder ran
  # (all three on a release run); read with a default of all three, so an
  # output that went missing compares more, never less.
ci.yml.bundle-identical:
name: bundle identical across OSes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    needs: [plan, test]
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'bundle-identical')
    env:
      LADDER_OSES: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.ladder_oses || 'ubuntu macos windows' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: bundle-manifest-*
      - name: compare the manifests byte-for-byte
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          ls -R
          set -- $LADDER_OSES
          if [ "${1:-}" != ubuntu ] || [ "$#" -lt 2 ]; then
            echo "::error::the ladder OSes are '$LADDER_OSES': ubuntu and at least one other, or there is nothing to compare"
            exit 1
          fi
          shift
          for os in "$@"; do
            if ! diff bundle-manifest-ubuntu-latest/MANIFEST.json \
                      "bundle-manifest-$os-latest/MANIFEST.json"; then
              echo "::error::the $os bundle differs from the linux one — a normalization regression; the per-file hashes above name the culprits"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "the bundles of $LADDER_OSES are hash-identical:"
          grep '"bundle_sha256"' bundle-manifest-ubuntu-latest/MANIFEST.json

  # The independence doctrine as a CI law: no wolf-lang code, ever.
ci.yml.independence:
name: independence
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'independence')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show active-toolchain

      - name: Lock file names no wolf crate and no wolf-lang git dependency
        run: |
          cargo generate-lockfile
          if grep -nE '^name = "wolf[-_]' Cargo.lock | grep -v '"wolf-interp"'; then
            echo "::error::Cargo.lock depends on a wolf-* crate; wolf-interp shares no code with the compiler."
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -n 'wolf-lang' Cargo.lock; then
            echo "::error::Cargo.lock has a dependency on the wolf-lang repository."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Only spec/ and corpus/ are consumed from the pin
        run: |
          if grep -rEn 'upstream/(crates|xtask|src)' \
               --include='*.rs' --include='*.toml' --include='*.yml' \
               --exclude-dir=target --exclude-dir=upstream --exclude-dir=.git . ; then
            echo "::error::Something reaches into upstream/ outside spec/ and corpus/."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: The pin is a recorded revision, not a moving branch
        run: |
          git submodule status --cached upstream
          test -n "$(git rev-parse HEAD:upstream)"

      # The frontend was written from spec/01 alone. Naming a compiler crate in
      # prose is fine and sometimes necessary ("deliberately not a mirror of
      # wolf_ast"); *importing* one is the doctrine breaking. This catches the
      # import, which the Cargo.lock check above cannot see for a path or
      # vendored dependency.
      - name: No source file imports a compiler-side crate
        run: |
          if grep -rEn '^\s*(pub )?use +wolf_(?!interp)|^\s*extern crate +wolf_' \
               -P --include='*.rs' \
               --exclude-dir=target --exclude-dir=upstream --exclude-dir=.git . ; then
            echo "::error::A source file imports a wolf-lang crate; the frontend is written from spec/ only."
            exit 1
          fi

  # wolf-lang#447, the lupin half: the linux archive must start on the oldest
  # glibc the project states (2.35, Ubuntu 22.04). `release.yml` builds its
  # linux archives on 22.04 and gates the floor with `ci/glibc-floor.sh`, but
  # release.yml only runs at a tag — so this job builds the SAME archive the
  # same way on every PR, unpacks it, runs a program from it, and measures the
  # floor on the shipped binary. A green here is the pre-tag proof; the
  # release job re-measures on the archive it uploads.
ci.yml.dist-floor:
name: dist floor (${{ matrix.os }})
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'dist-floor')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-22.04-arm]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show active-toolchain

      - name: build
        run: cargo build --release --locked

      - name: the glibc floor
        run: ci/glibc-floor.sh target/release/lupin

      # The native entropy row and the wasm cfg arms are small gates on the
      # already-allocated x86 runner: no additional job or matrix slot.
      - name: the OS entropy witnesses
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-22.04' && !cancelled()
        run: cargo test --release --locked --test os_random_is80 -- --nocapture

      - name: the wasm library is warning-free
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-22.04' && !cancelled()
        run: |
          rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
          cargo clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib --locked -- -D warnings

      # The archive release.yml would upload, unpacked where a user would
      # unpack it, running a program. `--version` alone proves nothing
      # (wolf-lang#447's second defect was a correct version string over a
      # tier that could not run).
      - name: archive, unpack and smoke a hello
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -1)
          target=$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')
          stem="lupin-${version}-${target}"
          mkdir -p "target/dist/${stem}"
          cp target/release/lupin README.md LICENSE CHANGELOG.md "target/dist/${stem}/"
          tar -C target/dist -czf "target/dist/${stem}.tar.gz" "${stem}"
          work="$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke"
          rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
          tar -xzf "target/dist/${stem}.tar.gz" -C "$work"
          ci/glibc-floor.sh "$work/${stem}/lupin"
          printf 'fn main() -> !int {\n    print("hello, wolf")\n    0\n}\n' > "$work/hello.lu"
          out=$("$work/${stem}/lupin" run "$work/hello.lu")
          test "$out" = "hello, wolf" \
            || { echo "::error::the unpacked binary did not print the hello: $out"; exit 1; }
          sha256sum "target/dist/${stem}.tar.gz"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dist-floor-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: target/dist/*.tar.gz
          retention-days: 14

  # The verdict (tl21), last: named for the tier the plan chose, and red
  # unless the plan succeeded, the jobs it chose are that tier's, every one
  # of them succeeded and every other job was skipped (`ci/tiers.py
  # verdict`). `!cancelled()`, never `always()`: under `always()` a
  # superseded run keeps this job queued after its other jobs are cancelled,
  # which holds the concurrency group and leaves the newer run pending
  # behind it (pax run 38275354849).
  #
  # A red NIGHTLY opens an issue (is78, ruling #92 R2): the windows heavy
  # shards and ladder run only there and at tier release, so the nightly's
  # red must reach a lane, not wait in the Actions tab. `ci/nightly-red.py`
  # names the red jobs and opens `nightly red: tier release on trunk`
  # (label `nightly-red`), or comments on it while it is open; the next lane
  # on wolf-interp owes it before its own merge. Only a `schedule` run: a
  # lane's own red is its own to read. The job's token may write issues and
  # read the run's jobs, nothing else.
ci.yml.tier:
name: tier ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tier || 'unplanned' }}
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs:
      - plan
      - plan-test
      - test
      - shard-coverage
      - bundle-identical
      - independence
      - dist-floor
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: every chosen job succeeded, every other was skipped
        env:
          NEEDS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: python3 ci/tiers.py verdict

      - name: a red nightly opens an issue
        if: failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          TIER: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tier || 'unplanned' }}
        run: python3 ci/nightly-red.py

release.yml.dist:
name: dist (${{ matrix.target }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Four tier-1 hosts, plus static musl x86-64 for PAX and libc-free hosts.
        # The two linux archives build on 22.04 — the oldest image GitHub
        # offers — so their glibc floor is 2.35 (wolf-lang#447, the lupin
        # half): 0.1.38's, built on ubuntu-latest (24.04), imported
        # GLIBC_2.39 through two weak symbols Rust std's spawn path links
        # when the build host's libc has them (`pidfd_spawnp`,
        # `pidfd_getpid`), and did not start on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS at all.
        # wolf 0.2.16 moved the same way (wolf-lang 0320443d). The step
        # `the glibc floor` below measures it on the binary that ships.
        include:
          - {os: ubuntu-22.04, target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu}
          - {os: ubuntu-22.04-arm, target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu}
          - {os: macos-latest, target: aarch64-apple-darwin}
          - {os: windows-latest, target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc}
          - {os: ubuntu-22.04, target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    env:
      TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # Full history AND tags: `build.rs` reads `git tag --points-at HEAD` to
      # decide the D57 stamp, and a shallow tag-only fetch does not always
      # leave the tag readable that way.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show active-toolchain

      - name: Toolchain versions
        run: |
          rustc --version
          cargo --version

      # The tag must be visible to git AND must be this crate's own release
      # tag, or the stamp below cannot be granted. Say so here rather than
      # letting the assertion fail with a confusing message.
      - name: The tag is at HEAD
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          git fetch --force --tags --quiet
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -1)
          echo "crate version: $version"
          echo "tag pushed:    ${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          test "v${version}" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            || { echo "::error::tag ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} does not match Cargo.toml v${version}"; exit 1; }
          git tag --points-at HEAD | grep -qx "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            || { echo "::error::${GITHUB_REF_NAME} does not point at HEAD in this checkout — the D57 stamp cannot be granted"; exit 1; }

      # The dist build is the stamped build (never a plain `cargo build` from
      # somewhere else): `build.rs` runs here, at the tag, and only here.
      - name: Install the musl target
        if: matrix.target == 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'
        run: rustup target add "$TARGET"

      - name: build
        run: |
          if [ "$TARGET" = x86_64-unknown-linux-musl ]; then
            ci/musl-build.sh
          else
            cargo build --release --locked --target "$TARGET"
          fi

      - name: the static ELF contract and digest
        if: matrix.target == 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'
        run: ci/musl-check.sh "target/${TARGET}/release/lupin"

      - name: the D57 stamp is on this binary
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          if [ "${RUNNER_OS}" = "Windows" ]; then
            bin=target/${TARGET}/release/lupin.exe
          else
            bin=target/${TARGET}/release/lupin
          fi
          out=$("$bin" --version)
          echo "$out"
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -1)
          case "$out" in
            *"+dev."*)
              echo "::error::the release build carries the dev suffix — D57 refused the stamp on ${{ matrix.os }}: $out"
              exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$out" in
            "lupin ${version} "*) ;;
            *) echo "::error::--version does not name the release: $out"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

      # The floor, measured on the binary that ships rather than assumed from
      # the runner (wolf-lang#447): the highest GLIBC symbol version it
      # imports, printed, and held at the 2.35 floor README states. A weak
      # reference counts — the loader refuses a missing version node whether
      # or not the symbol is weak, which is exactly how 0.1.38 failed.
      - name: the glibc floor
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && matrix.target != 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'
        run: ci/glibc-floor.sh "target/${TARGET}/release/lupin"

      # Archive layout: one directory, so an unpack cannot scatter files into
      # the user's cwd. `.zip` on Windows and `.tar.gz` everywhere else — the
      # convention each platform's users already have a tool for.
      - name: build archive
        id: archive
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -1)
          target="$TARGET"
          stem="lupin-${version}-${target}"
          mkdir -p "target/dist/${stem}"
          if [ "${RUNNER_OS}" = "Windows" ]; then
            cp target/${TARGET}/release/lupin.exe "target/dist/${stem}/"
          else
            cp target/${TARGET}/release/lupin "target/dist/${stem}/"
          fi
          cp README.md LICENSE CHANGELOG.md "target/dist/${stem}/"
          cd target/dist
          if [ "${RUNNER_OS}" = "Windows" ]; then
            7z a -tzip "${stem}.zip" "${stem}" >/dev/null
            echo "archive=target/dist/${stem}.zip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            tar -czf "${stem}.tar.gz" "${stem}"
            echo "archive=target/dist/${stem}.tar.gz" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "stem=${stem}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # The smoke: unpack the archive the way a user would, in a directory
      # that is not the checkout, and run a program with the unpacked binary.
      # `vendor/upstream/PIN` is baked in at compile time, so the unpacked
      # binary is self-contained and this proves it — a `--version` that
      # needed the repo beside it would fail right here.
      - name: unpack and smoke a hello
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          work="$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke"
          rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
          cp "${{ steps.archive.outputs.archive }}" "$work/"
          cd "$work"
          if [ "${RUNNER_OS}" = "Windows" ]; then
            7z x "$(basename '${{ steps.archive.outputs.archive }}')" >/dev/null
            bin="./${{ steps.archive.outputs.stem }}/lupin.exe"
          else
            tar -xzf "$(basename '${{ steps.archive.outputs.archive }}')"
            bin="./${{ steps.archive.outputs.stem }}/lupin"
          fi
          printf 'fn main() -> !int {\n    print("hello, wolf")\n    0\n}\n' > hello.lu
          "$bin" --version
          out=$("$bin" run hello.lu)
          echo "$out"
          test "$out" = "hello, wolf" \
            || { echo "::error::the unpacked ${{ matrix.os }} binary did not print the hello: $out"; exit 1; }

      # The learners' direct link (wolf-web ww09): the bare executable beside
      # the archive, so a page can point at one URL and get a runnable file.
      - name: the bare windows executable
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: cp target/${TARGET}/release/lupin.exe "target/dist/lupin.exe"

      # Five jobs upload to one release, so creation is a RACE: the
      # `upload-or-else-create` shape the upstream stub uses lets the loser of
      # that race drop its assets on the floor, which on this repo would mean
      # losing exactly the windows one this lane exists for. Create first,
      # tolerating "already exists", then upload unconditionally.
      #
      # Not a draft: ww09 needs a link that resolves, and a draft release's
      # assets are not publicly fetchable.
      - name: upload to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          assets=("${{ steps.archive.outputs.archive }}")
          if [ "${RUNNER_OS}" = "Windows" ]; then
            assets+=("target/dist/lupin.exe")
          fi
          if ! gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --title "lupin ${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" \
              --notes "Release notes: see [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/blob/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}/CHANGELOG.md)." \
